# Plan DAG

**Performance rule for every code agent (the author's order of 2026-11-05).** Every agent that writes or changes code must pass a performance test showing that the code is O(1), O(n) or O(n log n), or O(n log N) where O(n) is not possible (the author's decision of 2026-11-04). It may not exhibit O(n²) or worse without the author's explicit approval. An agent that finds such a cost must look for a better solution first, and if it cannot find one, must ask the author what to do. An item is not done until this holds. This rule applies to every item before Zed0 and after it, and no item has an edge for it. The test runs at n and 8n with inputs built before timing and stays within 24x, and a negative control that is run but not committed shows that it fails on a slower version. Code that is obviously O(1) instead carries a `// O(1):` comment giving the reason. The item SCALE-cover delivers the tool that fails the local test suite when code has neither.

This file lists the remaining work on Zed and the order it must run in. It has 2551 items, 3322 edges and 115 levels (0 to 114). It covers the TODO items, the store fixes, the left-recursion work, the T14 and T11 findings and every unchecked step in `../zed/PROGRESS.md`.

**Needs relaxed on 2026-11-02.** Items now run in parallel in their own worktrees, and a merge resolves a small overlap in a file. So the `needs` column keeps only three kinds of edge: code (one item uses or changes code the other writes), measure (one item measures code the other changes) and files-heavy (both rewrite the same functions). Edges of the other kinds were dropped: files-light (the same file, different functions), order (a preferred order with no technical cause), docs (one item only reads the other's text) and none (no reason found). Of the 1134 edges classified, 907 were code, 109 measure, 13 files-heavy, 52 files-light, 35 order, 3 docs and 15 none. Where the reviewer of the classification disagreed, its judgment was used. T11-fix was split into T11-fix-store and T11-fix-rest, X14 was added, and edges found missing were added after reading the cited code.

## How to read it

- An edge means one item needs another. The item in the first column cannot start until every id in its `needs` column is merged.
- The level of an item is the length of the longest path from a root, where a root is an item with no needs. Level 0 holds the roots.
- Two items with no directed path between them, in either direction, may run in parallel. Two items at the same level never have a path between them.
- Levels are a convenience. Items at different levels can also be unordered, and may then run in parallel. Use the `needs` column, not the level number, to decide.
- A file conflict is one item's path equal to, or inside a directory of, the other's. Since 2026-11-02 a file conflict between two items that the DAG does not order no longer forces an order: both may run, and the merge resolves the overlap. Run them apart where possible. The conflict lists compare paths as written, so they do not show a conflict through a glob, such as `tests/steps/*/scaling.rs` (T2 and SCALE-cover).
- An edge is added only when the code, a measurement or a rewrite of the same functions requires it. A missing edge of that kind costs a bad merge; an edge for a light file overlap costs parallel time and is left out.
- Reasons for the edges are in [Why each item waits](#why-each-item-waits). Where a reason or note disagrees with the `needs` column, the `needs` column wins, since the notes were written before the corrections below.

**Done, so not listed:** T1 (all crates optimized in dev builds, `Cargo.toml` `[profile.dev]` at `opt-level = 2`) and T8 (code in other languages removed). Both landed in commit cd2d30b. Every step L1.1 to L1.39 and M0.x is also done, so a need on one of them is treated as met and left out of the table. The exceptions are L1.17a, L1.29a, L1.37a, L1.39a and L1.39b, added on 2026-11-03, which have rows.

**Files every step touches:** `tests/Cargo.toml` (written by the step_targets tool), `tests/steps/m0_01_scaffolding/`, `STATUS.md`, `COMPLEXITY.md` and `../zed/PROGRESS.md`. These are left out of the conflict lists, since every pair would match. The changes are additive, so resolve them at merge by keeping both sides, then rerun step_targets and regenerate `PROGRESS.md`. Each step's own `tests/steps/lNN_MM_*/` directory is separate from every other step's.

**Builders of new forms.** A builder tells kids apart by the token that follows or by position, never by rule name where a `~` rule can stand (STATUS.md, the LR4 fix).

Fix: `Plan::halves` splits such a group by the ratio of each atom's coefficients (one ratio twice the other) into two groups whose sums are one number each, and `lattice` joins the two (a `Fused` pair) by meet in the middle on the words of their tables and interval arithmetic on their dense middles (Horowitz and Sahni 1974; Galil and Margalit 1991 for the density); a plan with a pair races with a doubling allowance from size·FIRST (Levin 1973). Other families against main, three runs each: many linked rows +0.43% at k = 512, a chain of overlapping sums +0.37% at k = 64 (open: PRES-pair-scan-cost), the rest within the spread of repeated runs. Negative control, run once: with growth off, the scaling test ran past 60 s. Left open: PRES-fused-bound, PRES-floor-grow, PRES-c12-proof. | 56 | SCHED-refined-store | Left open by SCHED-dep-dag: rule 3 of DESIGN sec:checking_in_zed, the refined store. Fix: the text is cut at NFC composition boundaries (UAX #15, "Stable Code Points"): before a character whose decomposition starts with a starter of quick check Yes, or a starter of quick check Maybe that does not compose with the last character of NFC of the piece so far; the span is the first piece that is not NFC. The inferred cause was right: `Comparing::search` gives a tuple piece to the first shape of `s` in written order that holds it, and `accepts` bound the first variable it found, so `(U,)` bound `B` (`for B in int \| f64`) in `(B,)`, which `bounds_hold` then refused. Fix (root cause, no third shortcut): `accepts` binds a variable only to a piece its bound holds, checked as `bounds_hold` checks it (`Binds::bound`, a binary search of the signature's bounds, shared by every copy of the binding; `var_mask`, `carrier_of`), so the shape does not hold the piece and the search goes on to `(U,)`. Only a piece known to lie outside the bound is refused: a carrier outside it, a variable of a known mask outside it (rigid, or a bounded own variable of an open comparison, `Cx::own_bounds`); a free or unbounded variable is checked as before. Outside every tuple shape (`Site::Other`) no other shape is searched, so a piece no variable admits is bound as before and `bounds_hold` names that binding in its message. `Cx::open` gives `s` its bounds under the names it reads them by. A rigid variable whose mask is one carrier counts as that carrier (`carrier_of`), so `T` bound to `V \| int` for `V in int` is one carrier. The two shortcuts of d20413aae (`read_alike`, `equal_fits`) stay: with either switched off a test fails (`a_bounded_variable_is_bound_only_to_what_its_bound_holds`, `signatures_with_a_variable_bound_in_a_tuple_fit_themselves_and_their_overloads`), each on an unbounded variable in the first shape, which a bound does not decide (row FAIL-types-first-shape-unbounded); this row's test passes with both off. The code was wrong, the test right: a held memo entry was reused on a higher stack, where reading the term again can enter a lambda that is active there and raise a Recursion stop. In the seed, v241 = App(v229, ..) is read inside Lam v242; v229's body reaches #3 again, which applies Lam v242, so reading again stops on it and the entry did not (an experiment that refused every held entry on a higher stack passed the seed). An entry is now (value, cut, high): `high` is the stack height it was made at when its read entered a lambda (`Run::entered` counts them), else usize::MAX, and a hit is reused only on a stack no higher than `high`; a hit with a finite `high` counts as entering a lambda. The exact rule needs the set of lambdas each read entered, O(l) per entry; the flag is O(1) per read and costs no read more than before. Tests: `entries_made_below_a_stop_give_what_reading_the_term_again_gives_seed_17213863407132117863` (red before); 399 of 400 random seeds of the entries and summaries tests passed, the one failure FAIL-preimage-summaries-rounds-seed. l01_25 benches (scaling, stops, shared): 26 pieces pass, ratios 3.5 to 8.9 apart from the n-squared `x * y mod 7 == 3` (46.1, 64 times the points). | 83 | HOST-embed | QUESTIONS Q38, answered by the author 2026-11-14 (zed commit 75cfe63; read the answer verbatim there): a C program drives a stateful Zed program directly. `@export` of such a program gives three C symbols: allocate (makes the state), tick (takes that state, a double pointer to a result and a result code saying whether the Zed function returned of its own accord before the C side called release) and release (frees the state; idempotent). Inside Zed the tick function takes an input stream and an output stream and does not return between ticks: its state is kept as a continuation and it yields to C each time its loop over the input stream waits for the next item. Results the output stream gives are allocated with malloc and freed by the C caller; the result pointer is set to null when a tick gives nothing. When the Zed function returns, its release runs at once and further ticks are invalid; after a release from C, further ticks are invalid. Do: (1) the sec:ffi paragraph beside the exports paragraph, with spec/grammar sync if `@export` syntax changes, and the sec:alternatives row correcting the Murail study's reason; (2) settle in DESIGN whether the result code is the tick's return value or an out-parameter, make a tick after release a defined, reported error (every catchable runtime error is caught), name the result type and its free function in the generated header, and state how the two streams meet the dynamic ports of Q51; (3) build it in libzed (no Rust after S.8); (4) tests: a C host allocates, ticks one item at a time and compares every output with the interpreter, the Zed side returning early (result code set, automatic release, tick after it refused), release called twice, release with no tick, a tick giving nothing (null result), results holding struct graphs freed by C under a leak checker. Added by the author the same day: `@export` names the path of a C header file to generate, and that header defines every struct of the object graphs the output stream can allocate and return (with the three functions and the result type); test that the header compiles with `cc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror` and that a host built only from it frees every result graph without a leak. Added by the author the same day (P195): every tick function compiles two ways. (a) The exported version, in the shared library with the C interface: its input-stream readers read the C caller's struct graphs in place and never free them, and the graphs it writes to the output stream are plain C layouts with no refcounts, written once in that form (no second copy made to strip refcounts). (b) When Zed code in the same program calls the tick function directly, a second version is compiled under Zed's normal refcounting and its stream fusion (state-machine or coroutine compilation), with the input stream fused to the caller and the output stream to the consumer, so no buffer or C graph is built. Both versions come from one definition and must agree: test each tick function both ways on the same inputs, comparing output values and counting allocations (the fused version allocates nothing the unfused one does not, and the exported one does no refcount operation). Cause: written by name, the printer unfolds a part kept unevaluated (`At::Part`) once, with no definition (`Printer::ty`); in the seed's system `R1 = R0 \ Never` unfolds to `R0`'s parts, the part `#a \| R0` unfolds to a tuple holding itself, so the texts formed a cycle with no defined recursive type on it, and `heights` stopped with a panic. The group builder was right: the system is admitted by DESIGN, and DESIGN sec:diagnostics has parts that use each other in a cycle defined together. A decimal literal that no use fixes takes f64 (reverses the 2026-11-09 rejection); an integer literal that no use fixes stays `int`, so `1 / 2`, `2 ^ -1` and `(3/2) ^ -2` with nothing fixing them stay refused, the exact repair first (`1r / 2`, `2r ^ -1`, `(3r / 2) ^ -2`), then the f64 one (`1.0 / 2`). A use that fixes a carrier fixes it for the literal, as for every literal since 2026-11-09: `r: rat = 0.5 ^ n` is accepted and exact, as `r: rat = 0.5` is (CHANGES the author request to refuse it; the repair `0.5r ^ n` is instead offered where an f64 `y = 0.5 ^ n` meets a rat use); `f: f32 = 0.5 ^ n` is f32. The exponent of `^` is the one exception to the rule that both operands of an arithmetic operation have one carrier: an `int` exponent goes with a base of any number carrier, `(int, int) -> int` (exponent proved non-negative), `(rat, int) -> rat`, `(F, int) -> F` at every float format F; a non-integer exponent needs one carrier, so the repair for a `rat` exponent `k` is `f64(x) ^ f64(k)`, and for a float one `f64(x) ^ k`; an int base literal beside a decimal exponent takes f64 (`2 ^ 0.5` is f64, no refusal). | 0 | SPEC-zero-order | DESIGN L1.17 orders numbers by exact value, then kind, then float format, and sec:order says a natural order's ties are exactly ==; so -0.0 and 0.0 (one rational, one format, -0.0 == 0.0) get one place. The kernel's natural order (crates/zed-kernel/src/value.rs:679-683 number_cmp, F64 Ord = total_cmp) puts -0.0 before 0.0, and must: Value's Eq is bitwise (the two zeros print differently and have different content addresses), and Rust's Ord must agree with Eq. Keys are not affected (key_leaf maps -0.0 to 0.0). Proposed DESIGN sentence for L1.17: two floats of one value and one format order -0.0 before 0.0, as IEEE totalOrder and min/max do. Then change the ignored test l01_17_value_representation::edges::the_two_float_zeros_tie_in_the_natural_order to expect Less and remove its ignore. Not unsound: no Zed program at L1 observes the natural order of non-key floats (no sort word; min/max have their own IEEE rule). Deferred tests: /home/luke/Work/wt/scratch/deferred-tests/SPEC-zero-order.rs, back into `tests/steps/l01_17_value_representation/edges.rs` when this step is done. | - | - | none |  |

Present on the branch at e58ddc11, before repair 5. Cause: the need f takes v is checked at the call by call_found with arguments Arg::of(..), at = None, so apply passes no atom by (rule 6 needs an argument span) and a lambda fitted as (String) -> String refuses #_. main rejects the same call on stdin[2] directly. Proposed: a need replayed at a call passes by the loose atoms the function value refuses, recorded at the call span of the higher-order call (elaboration then passes them at that call), or the widening keeps x unwidened in a body that only fails with it widened; needs a decision on whether pass-by at the outer call is the intended semantics | - | - | ISSUE1-else-atoms |  |

| 1 | PERF-l139-family | Superlinear growth on main in the L1.39 reduced product over ten families, each with an ignored scaling test in tests/steps/l01_39_reduced_product/families.rs (TESTS-lhx-families 8c8510fb0) as its red test: boxstar k^2.1, chain ~k^1.7 (passes only at n = 2), coordkk k^1.23-1.78, coordmix-floor k^1.8-2.2 (59G instructions at k = 64), coordmix-slopes ~k^2, hop ~k^2.05, persist k^2.5, stair-cover ~k^2, stair-holes k^2.0-2.8, star-extra k^1.75-1.96. Profile the ten together first (likely one shared cause in product.rs), fix, enable every test, then cross-review per the standing rule. Attempt 1 (2026-11-12): coordkk fixed and its test enabled (9.6 times the work from k = 16 to 128, limit 15.4; COMPLEXITY.md PERF-l139-due); coordmix-slopes was already enabled (LAZY-hub-unsolved). Open, eight families and fourteen tests, one shared cause found by profiling: boxstar, chain, coordmix-floor, hop (hop, hopon, hopb, hoponb), persist, stair-cover (stair_cover, stair_cover_free), stair-holes (stair_holes, stair_holes_mix, stair_holes_late), star-extra. Each move of a name's interval, mostly in the arm copies `cases` makes, projects again every part that mentions the name (`Scope::project_block` wakes `due_users`), near k parts almost none of which changes, so near k^1.7 to k^1.9 projections; stair-holes also pays near k per projection for the holes of `x`. Next: cross-review of a way to wake only the parts whose result can change. Attempt 2 (2026-11-13, PERF-l139-wake, COMPLEXITY.md PERF-l139-wake): a part already projected is not projected again when its block has an integer witness by Fourier-Motzkin elimination with the dark shadow on rows that never grow (`Scope::idle`), plus puncture, staircase and ray certificates; eleven tests enabled, ratios at 8n under 13 (stair_holes, stair_holes_mix, stair_cover, stair_cover_free under 9; stair_holes_late, hop, hopon, hoponb, boxstar, coordmix_floor, cuts 9 to 13). Open, four tests: star_extra 16.3 times the instructions (idle's elimination is O(k) per call over O(k) calls; next: keep the eliminated rows per block version and wake incrementally in `due_users`), persist 13.2 times the bytes, hopb 13.0 and chain 13.1 times the instructions. Attempt 3 (2026-11-14, COMPLEXITY.md PERF-l139-hull-real): each side of a hull is first asked at the real bound of its conjunction by Fourier-Motzkin on rows that never grow (`real_end` in presburger.rs `hull_side`); hop (8.9 and 8.5 at 8n) and hopon (9.8 and 9.4) run again; instructions and bytes at 8n now chain 10.7/10.3, hopb 10.8/10.3, hoponb 10.8/10.2, cuts 10.6/10.5, boxstar 10.9/10.3, coordmix_floor 10.9/9.9, star_extra 13.4/11.0, persist 21.5/20.6 (its work falls, 2,849M to 2,097M at k = 16, but less at the large end). Attempt 4 (b5299bd8b): `real_end` counts the sides of every atom again each round; persist allocates 16.6M and 227.7M bytes (39.4M and 516.7M before), 13.7 times; a cache of `Split::with` in `Block::reframe` measured equal and dropped. Open causes, for cross-review: (1) persist, each constraint joins the one {x, y} group and `Block::reframe` rebuilds `Split::new` and runs `bounds_at` for every part, O(k) each (PERF-l139-block-incr); (2) star_extra and boxstar, the `Scope::idle` checks grow as k^2, each test waking the O(k) parts that read the changed name, at a constant 27.6K instructions each; (3) boxstar, `project_by_pendants` and `project_each` grow 4.97 and 4.77 times per 4 times k; (4) chain, hopb, hoponb, cuts and coordmix_floor (10.7 to 11.3), hull-side questions still grow faster than linearly (persist: sides 834 to 3,522, questions 195 to 1,511; costly sides of the shape `x >= 21y + 1`, 8 or 11 questions each). XR-l139-family (f9936c4fe): a hull side over the symbol and one other atom, after unit equalities are substituted, is read off the envelopes of its rows (`twovar::ends`, `two_atom_side` in `hull_side`) with no question; cuts_scale (7.1 at 8n) and boxstar_scales (8.8) are back in families.rs; still deferred then: chain 10.9, coordmix_floor 12.0, hopb 11.2, hoponb 11.2, persist 15.3, star_extra 14.9 (instructions at 8n). XR-l139-family round 2 (fe5b3e683): the least part of a chain of disjunctions certifies the parts above it (`Scope::idle_by_chain`); coordmix_floor_scales (10.2), star_extra_scales (10.1) and chain_scales (10.2) are back; still deferred: hopb 11.2, hoponb 11.2, persist 13.9 (instructions at 8n). XR-l139-family round 3: Opus (1aff02482, COMPLEXITY.md C64: one shared formula per group, a known-empty bounds context skipped, due parts in a vector) and Gemini merged in part (16fe26be8 and 8818e910f, COMPLEXITY.md XR-l139-gemini: `with` as a persistent shared set, `Split::update` in place of `Split::new` at reframe, the bounds entries of a part on two names kept while which of their ends are finite holds, `certified_chains`, `free_two_base`); `hopb_scales` and `hoponb_scales` are back, in `tests/steps/l01_39_reduced_product/families/bench.rs` (benchmarks, run with --bench), at 9.85 and 9.87 times the instructions at 8n through `tools/run_tests.sh --bench`; still deferred: persist, 11.31 times the instructions and 10.70 the bytes (rows PERF-l139-persist-due and PERF-l139-block-incr); hopb and hoponb are over 9 and at n = 3 over 10.5 (PERF-l139-hopb-wakes). Build the exponent operation once per carrier as `elab::walk::per_carrier` does, with its marks in every arm, so the mutant replaces it at each arm (as MUTATE-generic-constants does for a constant) | - | - | STAGE-generic-fold-div |  |
| 7 | STAGE-generic-fold-int-arm | Done: the commit "STAGE-generic-fold-int-arm: ..." that marks this row Done. The checker accepts no program where an `int` reaches such a last arm (a decimal or a `/` removes `int` from the class, L1.26a), and the kernel has no operation on an `int` and another carrier nor `/` on two `int`s, so elaboration lays the two operands out on the patterns of the one whose last arm is at the other carrier `c` (`f64` for `/` on two `int`s), each taking its value at `c` in the new last arm (`elab::walk::without_int`, O(C²) per operation, C ≤ 4, arms moved, not copied); no value is given that the checker did not give. `x * (1 / 2 + 2 ^ 2 + 1)`, `x * ((1 + 1.5) + 0)` and `x * (1 / 2 + 0)` are one `match` (`FOLDED`), and `1 / 2 - 0` and the mutants of `(1 + 1.5) + 0` are skipped. Benches: the sum of quotients 7.95 times (128.9 to 1,024.3 million instructions at 2,000 and 16,000), the chain 8.00 times. Found by STAGE-generic-fold-div: an operation on generic literals alone whose last arm, at `int`, mixes carriers is still a `let` and a `match` per following literal: `x * (1 / 2 + 2 ^ 2 + 1)`, where `1 / 2` is a `rat` and `2 ^ 2` an `int` in that arm, and `x * ((1 + 1.5) + 0)`, a decimal and an integer. The value is unchanged, but the L25.8 mutation skip does not see the form folded, and in `x * (1 / 2 + 0)` the mutant `1 / 2 - 0` is reported undetected rather than skipped, since the build stage cannot build `int / int` in that arm (the kernel has no `/` on two `int`s). Fix: the checker gives those literals a carrier's value in the last arm, as it gives `1.0` in `x == 1 / 2`, or elaboration drops the last arm where the checker proves no `int` reaches it; test in `l01_26a_generic_literals::operations` (`NOT_FOLDED`) and `l25_08_mutate::examples::a_mutant_of_a_folded_decimal_or_power_is_skipped` | - | - | STAGE-generic-fold-div |  |

## File conflicts at the same level

Each pair below is at one level, shares a file and is not yet done. No path of needs joins two items at one level, since each level is one more than the highest level among the item's needs. Under the rule of 2026-11-02 the two may run in parallel and the merge resolves the overlap; run them apart where possible. There are 1323 pairs. This section and the next are written by `cargo run -q -p zed-tools --bin conflicts` from the items table above (with `--check` it only compares them with it); edit the table and rerun it, not the lists. Two items share a file when a path of one equals a path of the other or lies inside a directory path of the other, one that ends in `/`. Paths are compared as written, less a trailing ` (new)`; files under `tests/` and the files every step touches are not compared. The two items of a row are in the order of their rows in the table, and the shared paths are the longer path of each match.

## Machine limits and tools

The author installed the tools below on 2026-11-02. Each was run that day on a small input, and the versions are the ones reported. All tests stay under 60 s each and 112 GB in total. There are two test suites. The local suite, `tools/run_tests.sh`, needs only the Rust toolchain and the cores of the machine, and it is what CI runs: tests in `tests/steps/`. The full battery, `tools/run_tests.sh --full`, is the local suite plus `tests/full/<step>/`, each with a file `needs` listing its tools. It stops before any test and names what is missing, so nothing is skipped. `tools/fetch_test_deps.sh` fetches into `~/.cache/zed-test-deps`, with no root, what Fedora does not package: target sysroots, the official rustc for target builds, and Podman's test storage and image. Every test that uses a tool in this table goes in `tests/full/`, and a step with such tests runs `--full` before it merges. Plain `cargo test` does not build `tests/full/`; clippy in CI compiles it.

| Items | Tools and what was run | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| L21.1, L21.3 | PostgreSQL 18.6 (`initdb`, `pg_ctl`, a query), MariaDB 11.8.8 (`mariadb-install-db`, `mariadbd` as `mysqld`, a query), SQLite 3.51.2. | Run private instances as the user, in a temporary directory, on a socket with networking off. Do not use the system services. |
| L26.1 | `wasmtime` 50.0.1 from cargo, in `~/.cargo/bin`, which must be on `PATH`. Ran a module built with `clang --target=wasm32` and `wasm-ld`. | Use `wasmtime` for the cross-target tests. |
| L27.1 | RTX 3050, driver 615.78.08, Vulkan 1.4. `llvmpipe` software Vulkan is also present. | Run the GPU tests on the card locally. `llvmpipe` gives a software device where no GPU exists. |
| L27.2 | Multi-host behavior runs on one machine. Rootless Podman 5.8.9 with `crun` 1.28: two containers on a private network reached each other, and `podman kill` (0.1 s), `pause`, and `network disconnect` and `connect` worked. A paused container's processes stop, but its kernel still answers ping, so a pause test must watch the protocol, not ping. A container starts in 1.5 s. A veth pair between user network namespaces with `tc netem` delayed packets, which needs no root. KVM (`/dev/kvm`, `qemu-system-x86_64`) is also present. | Each node is a rootless Podman container, with the storage from `tools/fetch_test_deps.sh`. Stopping a machine is `podman kill`, pausing one past its lease is `podman pause`, a partition is `podman network disconnect`. Delay and loss use `netem` on a veth pair. Use a KVM VM only for what a container cannot show, such as a kernel crash. Do not use Docker. |
| L27.3 | Yosys 0.67 (synthesis of a small module), Verilator 5.046 (lint), Icarus Verilog 13.0 (simulation). | Use these. |
| L28.1, L28.2 | `mlir-opt`, `mlir-translate`, `llc`, `opt` and `wasm-ld`, all LLVM 22.1.8, matching `clang`. Lowered a small module from MLIR through `llc`. | Use these. |
| L29.1, L29.2 | `qemu-aarch64` and `qemu-riscv64` 10.2.2, `clang`, `lld`, and gdb 18.1, which reads both targets. With the sysroots from `tools/fetch_test_deps.sh`, C, C++, static C and Rust programs ran under qemu on both targets, gdb stopped at a breakpoint through `qemu -g`, and `zed-rt` built for aarch64 with the official rustc 1.99.1. | Link with `~/.cache/zed-test-deps/bin/<arch>-cc`, run with `qemu-<arch> -L ~/.cache/zed-test-deps/<arch>/usr/<arch>-linux-gnu`, and build target Rust with `~/.cache/zed-test-deps/rust/bin/rustc`. Fedora's rustc rejects the official target std with E0514. `tests/full/s00_01_tools/` shows each command. |
| L30.1, L30.6 | `code`, node v22, `Xvfb` and `xvfb-run` (ran a command under `xvfb-run`). | Run headless editor tests under `xvfb-run -a`. |
| L5.14, L23.5 | Timing runs must not share the 32 cores with other branches. | Run these alone, with no parallel branch active. |
| L7.15 | The 10 GB demo must fit the 112 GB and 60 s caps. | Size the run to fit, and report the size used. |
| L19.3 | The run takes over 60 s. | Split it per program. |
| XE2 | Codex and `agy` logins; `agy`'s three environment variables. | Running now. If a login fails, report it. |

CI has none of these tools and runs only the local suite, so each item in this table puts the tests that use them in `tests/full/`. Timing tests can fail when other work loads the machine (5 pieces failed at load 57 on 32 cores and passed when rerun alone), so read a failure under load by rerunning the piece before calling it a regression.

## Why each item waits

- **T2-eval.** No needs. *Note:* on_stack is called at product.rs:1281,1508,1637 and preimage.rs:170,2204,2225,2294, so removing it touches product.rs; do that part after ST1 or keep on_stack as a thin no-op until T2-mid deletes it. Keeping the no-op wrapper is the recommended way to avoid an edge to ST1 and ST2. *Note:* MAX_DEPTH was the hidden limit set by the thread stack. The complexity rule and the quadratic-to-lookup rule require a better form (index arrows by universe and head constructor), or a stated reason beside the code; hence hard. Spec gap: when arrow choice stays dynamic, the dispatch term is unspecified; recommended a Term::Match over Pattern::Is in rank order, with a static arrow when the type settles it, so no new kernel term or ZIR op is added. Pattern::Is rejects types that bound functions (L1.22), so dispatch on a function-typed domain must be static or rejected. The merged failure's static type is `#errs(E ->? E)`, `E` the union of the operands' loose failures with the members of an operand's own `#errs` flattened in, so a chain holds one `#errs` and never a nested one; it prints with `E` written out and parses back to the same type (`{…}` in a type holds literals only, sec:grammar `SetType`, so DESIGN's `#errs({E})` was not type syntax; the spec branch writes `#errs(E ->? E)` at its three type uses). An operand whose `#errs` members are not known makes the merge's members unknown, `#errs(..)`; `outside_of` and `unnamed_of` still add `#errs(..)`, which is sound but wider. Building `E` along a chain made `Atoms::zip` in the kernel walk the whole smaller map at each step, O(n²) for n different failures; it now also walks the diff of the two maps, which skips the nodes they share (COMPLEXITY.md F101). allOk (DESIGN.md:513) is not part of this item; row L3.2 builds it, as DESIGN step L3.2 (DESIGN.md:2015) and the layer table (DESIGN.md:4091) say; the orchestrator's assignment of 2026-11-05 to L2.7 was wrong. - **PRODUCT-nested-chain.** Needs ST-arms-quad, ST-formula-share, ST-ladder, F70-rerun (the measured cause, added 2026-11-05). *Option (a), 2026-11-05, from the study of Adams et al. 2011 (wt/study-linearlog/REPORT.md, candidate B; their section 3.2 reads each node once, bottom up) as fitted to F70-rerun's measurement (COMPLEXITY F70):* `arms` itself does little here. The outer test `(if … ) == 1` is one atom, and `preimage::linear` turns the whole nest into one relation, a nest of d disjunctions linked through `n`. `presburger::project_parts` then calls `settle_as_sets` once per level, about d^2 disjuncts are solved in all, and each solve takes the whole linked base (`Linked::around`, about 0.65d rows): d^3. The fix keeps each inner `if` as a summary computed once, bottom up: for each outcome of its test, the product of its value (the interval set of `n` on that arm and the arm's linear value) and the scope on that outcome. The preimage of the level above reads the summary in place of the inner relation, so each level costs O(1) summaries and the nest O(d). The same summary serves `Scope::cases` where an inner `if` is a node of the test's `Tree`. Wherever a summary widens a hull that the exact projection keeps, put a `// Complexity tradeoff:` comment at that site. The comment names the inputs whose hull widens, says why (the exact projection settles every level against the whole linked base, d^3), names the trigger (an `if` nested inside a compared value), and names this row's test and COMPLEXITY F70. On the measured family each summary is exact and of constant size (true arm `n` in `[1..=1]` with value `n`, false arm `n` in `[..=0, 2..]` with value `2n`), so option (a) reaches O(d); a nest whose arms' interval sets grow with depth makes the summaries grow too, and the test at d and 8d must then still hold. *Considered and not adopted (F70-rerun merge check, 2026-11-05):* (b) give each disjunct only the base rows linked to its own atoms by a union-find over shared atoms. `Linked` is already that union-find, and every row of this nest mentions `n`; counters showed about one group per solve and 97 to 99% of the base rows handed over, so (b) removes nothing, score 0 of 10. (c) An incremental solve against a base kept solved: the d^2 solves remain, so O(d^2) at best, score 2 of 10. Option (a), O(d) on this family, score 8 of 10 (minus for the hulls it may widen elsewhere). *Note:* Ledger queued with feeds L1.40, T12 and no plan row, so plan_dag.md:31-32's rule failed until this row. COMPLEXITY F70 says not fixed, rerun 2026-11-05 by F70-rerun: Θ(d^3). ST-arms-quad fixed another cost on deep conditions. The earlier figure, about d^2.4 (76 MB at d = 16 to 1.2 GB at d = 48), came from small d. *Test:* The `chain` input of tests/steps/l01_39_reduced_product/follow.rs:84 at d and 8d within 24x in time and bytes; today's code is the negative control; arms equal. Also: Same answers as now on the corpus and random inputs. Scaling: n and 8n within 24x. Corner: depth 48. Negative control, run once and never committed: the old arms must exceed 24x. *Changed 2026-11-07 (DAG-fanin):* needs implied by a longer path dropped, each reason above still holding through the path named: ST-arms-quad (via ST-ladder). *Needs now:* ST-ladder, ST-formula-share, F70-rerun.

Unobservable to programs, so placing it before S.1 costs order only. *Integer ranges (author, 2026-11-09):* a union of one or more atoms with an integer domain that does not fill its word stores the atoms in unused values of the word instead of a separate tag, so the value is not a pair (number, atom). The atoms take the bit patterns of -1, -2, and so on down, the old convention: in a signed word these are -1 and -2, in an unsigned word its largest values (255 and 254 in `u8`). Where the domain holds those patterns (`int[-5..<100]`), the atoms take the values just past the domain's other end. The test for an atom is then one comparison with the domain's bound, and a `match` over the atoms is one jump table. Where the word has fewer unused values than atoms, a separate tag is kept, with a `// Complexity tradeoff:` comment if a wider word was weighed. *Test:* `int[0..=254] | #none` in a narrow column is one byte; `f64 | #none` is eight; `int[0..<100] | #unknown | #bad` is one byte, with `#unknown` and `#bad` stored as 255 and 254 in `u8`, and as -1 and -2 in `i8` when the domain is `int[0..<100]` in a signed column; `int[-5..<100] | #unknown | #bad` uses 100 and 101; `int[0..=255] | #none` keeps a tag. Differential test: every value and atom round-trips through the packed form. Corner cases: no spare value left; foreign and grammar formats excluded. Scaling: layout choice at n and 8n members within 24x. Negative control, run once and never committed: make the spare value collide with a real value and require the differential test to fail. - **L1.40b-sparse.** L1.40a: the cell as a table of layers, whose scope the facts are kept in. *Note:* Added 2026-11-05 from the study of Adams, Keep, Midtgaard, Might, Chauhan and Dybvig, "Flow-Sensitive Type Recovery in Linear-Log Time", OOPSLA 2011 (wt/study-linearlog/REPORT.md, candidate A). The paper proves (p7, Fig. 10) that an analysis giving each expression a full environment, and one for each outcome of a test, is O(n²). Today the checker narrows only the names a test mentions and restores them (`check/mod.rs`), and a join of two `Scope`s walks only what the arms changed (`store/product.rs`, `Scope::join`); L1.40b must keep that shape when the checker reads the store. The paper's own O(n log n) method (section 4) does not carry over, since relations between names break its guard property and the lattices have unbounded height. Feeds L1.40b. *Test:* k names and d nested tests, each test mentioning one name, at k = d; bytes and instructions at n and 8n within 24x, with the inputs built before timing. Negative control, run once and not committed: a version that copies the whole environment at each test must exceed 24x.

- **NAME-nonprinting.** Needs TESTS-L1.1-invisible. *Changed 2026-11-12:* NAME-ascii-only makes every name ASCII, so no such character can be in a name; the tables and the code-point message stay for code and for words beyond ASCII. *Note:* Added 2026-11-12 from the author's answer to QUESTIONS A97 ("Don't allow nonprinting characters in names.", zed 0ef0fd7). After the author's follow-up (byte order marks, no-break spaces and other characters used in composition), the set is Default_Ignorable_Code_Point plus the three characters of XID_Start or XID_Continue whose glyph is blank but which lack that property, U+13441 and U+13442 (Egyptian hieroglyph blanks) and U+16FE4 (Khitan small script filler); outside names `Space` already admits only U+0020, tab and the line breaks. The messages name by its code point every character of the general categories Cc, Cf, Zs, Zl, Zp, Co, Cs and Cn, every White_Space character, every character of no width and every character a name may not hold. The set is the Unicode property Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, wider than the joiners A97 asked about; the Hangul fillers are XID_Start letters, so the rule covers a name's first character. The grammar engine runs `XID_START` and `XID_CONTINUE` as code (crates/zedc-syntax/src/parse/engine.rs), so the PEG class, the engine and the lexer change together. *Test:* each Default_Ignorable character inside a name and at its start is an error at its span with the code-point message; each is accepted in a comment and in string text; `a_zero_width_joiner_or_non_joiner_inside_a_name_is_part_of_it` becomes a test of the error; a check that the table of excluded characters equals the property in the Unicode data the lexer's other tables use.

So `f(positional n: int) { x = if n > 0 { #e() } else { 7 }; return if x is #e { "bare" } else { x }; }` was typed `(int) -> 7 | #e()` and returned `"bare"` for 1.
